This page is the schema of the `EvalSuite` custom resource, one of the two the assayd chart installs.

**`Agent` and `EvalSuite` are the whole API surface the chart ships today.** `make manifests` produces two CRDs,
each rendered to a page of its own:

- `Agent`, from `api/v1alpha1/agent_types.go`: `docs/reference/crd-agent.md`
- `EvalSuite`, from `api/v1alpha1/evalsuite_types.go`: `docs/reference/crd-evalsuite.md`

The chart ships every one of them in `charts/assayd/crds/`, byte-identical to what
`make manifests` generates. The generator checks the set of generated CRDs before writing these
pages and refuses to write them if any other appears, so the sentence cannot outlive the fact.
(Each kind's `List` type carries the same root marker and is the list type of its CRD, not
another one.) Documentation elsewhere that counts more assayd CRDs is describing designs, not this
build.

**Defaults are applied by the API SERVER, not by the operator.** Every `Default` below comes from a
`+kubebuilder:default` marker, which controller-gen writes into the structural schema as
`default:`. The API server substitutes it on write, so the value is present on the stored object
and in `kubectl get -o yaml` whether or not the field was typed. A field with no `Default` row is
absent when it is not set, and the operator's own behaviour for an absent field is described in
that field's text, not here.

**The field tables do NOT list every validation rule. [Every validation rule](#every-validation-rule)
does.** The tool that renders the tables emits a `Validations` row for object-typed fields only —
never for an array item's schema, and never for the root — so of this CRD's 8 rules on 6 schema
nodes the tables carry 5 nodes' worth. A field with no `Validations` row in a table is therefore
NOT a field with no rules. The complete list is read out of the CRD itself and its presence on this
page is checked before the page is written.

**Required is the schema's `required` list**, not "the operator needs it". A field marked

## assayd.dev/v1alpha1

Resource Types:

- [EvalSuite](#evalsuite)




### EvalSuite
<sup><sup>[↩ Parent](#assayddevv1alpha1 )</sup></sup>






EvalSuite is the set of cases a gated Agent's candidate revision must pass
before it takes traffic (design 16 §1.1). The chart's admission policy
assayd-evalsuite-writers admits a create or update only from a principal
that may update Agents in the suite's namespace, namespace-wide.

#### EvalSuite.spec
<sup><sup>[↩ Parent](#evalsuite)</sup></sup>



EvalSuiteSpec is design 16 §1.1's slice of the EvalSuite: a list of cases,
at most one metric, and a per-case timeout. It is a strict subset of design
16 §3's schema (Q8 (a)), so the full schema can add fields without migrating
a stored suite. Every other §3 field — runner, target, dataset.goldenSetRef,
dataset.fromSessions, gate, budget — is absent, and the API server prunes or
refuses it as it does any unknown field.

An Agent binds a suite through spec.gates[].evalSuiteRef, in the Agent's own
namespace; the suite names no Agent.

The operator's eval controller sends each case to a gated candidate and
writes the verdict to the Agent's status.eval. The Agent reconciler reads
the suite a gate names and promotes a candidate only once status.eval
records a Passed verdict for it against this suite's digest, with its card
recorded; until then it holds, under GatesPassed=False/EvalRunning while the
run goes on.

## Every validation rule

All 8 `x-kubernetes-validations` rules in the CRD, on all 6 schema nodes that carry any.

**This section, and not the field tables above, is the complete list.** The tables carry a
`Validations` row for object-typed fields only: an ARRAY ITEM schema's rules and the root
schema's do not appear there at all, so a field with no `Validations` row in a table is not a
field with no rules. The generator reads every rule out of the CRD itself and fails rather than
writing this page if any of them is missing from it.

Each rule is CEL, evaluated by the API server on every write, and a write that fails one is
REFUSED with the message beside it. `self` is the node the rule sits on.

### Rules on `EvalSuite.spec.dataset.cases`

[Fields of `EvalSuite.spec.dataset`](#evalsuitespecdataset)

```cel
self.size() >= 1
```

> spec.dataset.cases is empty, and an eval with no cases would pass every revision. Add at least one case: {id, message, expect: {contains or equals}}.

```cel
self.all(c, self.exists_one(d, d.id == c.id))
```

> spec.dataset.cases[].id must be unique within the suite: each case's outcome is recorded by its id. Rename the duplicate.

### Rules on `EvalSuite.spec.dataset.cases[index]`

[Fields of `EvalSuite.spec.dataset.cases[index]`](#evalsuitespecdatasetcasesindex)

```cel
(!has(self.expect.contains) || !self.message.contains(self.expect.contains)) && (!has(self.expect.equals) || self.message != self.expect.equals)
```

> this case's message already satisfies its own expectation, so an agent that echoes its input would pass it. Change the expectation to something only a correct answer contains.

### Rules on `EvalSuite.spec.metrics[index].name`

[Fields of `EvalSuite.spec.metrics[index]`](#evalsuitespecmetricsindex)

```cel
self == 'task_completion'
```

> spec.metrics[].name must be task_completion: it is the only metric in this release (design 16 §1.1).

### Rules on `EvalSuite.spec.metrics[index].threshold`

[Fields of `EvalSuite.spec.metrics[index]`](#evalsuitespecmetricsindex)

```cel
self.matches('^(0([.][0-9]{1,3})?|1([.]0{1,3})?)$')
```

> spec.metrics[].threshold must be a decimal string from 0 to 1 with at most three decimal places, such as 0.66 or 1.

```cel
!self.matches('^0([.]0{1,3})?$')
```

> spec.metrics[].threshold must be greater than 0: a threshold of 0 would pass every revision.

### Rules on `EvalSuite.spec.dataset.cases[index].expect`

[Fields of `EvalSuite.spec.dataset.cases[index].expect`](#evalsuitespecdatasetcasesindexexpect)

```cel
has(self.contains) != has(self.equals)
```

> spec.dataset.cases[].expect must set exactly one of contains or equals.

### Rules on `EvalSuite.spec.dataset.cases[index].id`

[Fields of `EvalSuite.spec.dataset.cases[index]`](#evalsuitespecdatasetcasesindex)

```cel
self.matches('^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$')
```

> spec.dataset.cases[].id must be a DNS label: lowercase letters, digits and '-', starting and ending with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters.
